model.name: UAV printed 2-element collinear (867 MHz)
model.description: Printed two-element collinear on a slim vertical FR-4 strip (1.6 mm, board in the xz plane, z up), with no ground plane, for a UAV with a non-metal (composite) fuselage. The lower element is the self-balancing sleeve dipole of sleeve_dipole_867 (an arm, a sleeve of two strips either side of the coax braid strip, joined to it by a bridge at the top). A meander phasing section of six turns at the top of the arm reverses the current, so a second, end-fed half-wave element above it radiates in phase with the dipole (0.61 wavelengths apart). The collinear's feed point is about 200 ohm, so a quarter-wave strip-pair line (a 1.2 mm trace on the back face behind the 1.2 mm braid strip, about 116 ohm) transforms it to 50 ohm: the 50 ohm lumped port sits at the lower end of that line, where the coax ends, and a via joins the trace to the arm at the feed gap. Vertically polarised and omnidirectional in azimuth for the 863-870 MHz SRD / LoRa band, with about 2 dB more gain on the horizon than a half-wave dipole and a 39 degree elevation beam. See examples/designs/README.md in the fairbeam repository.
